b.answer:
Worked example: Harvest Lane's Boss 4 agent split into one brain and a Telegram adapter.

SUB · Sage Desk brain (new workflow)

  1. Sub-workflow trigger (When Executed by Another Workflow) with three inputs: channel, user_id, text.
  2. AI Agent: Boss 4's system message, tools and guardrails, unchanged. Memory session key = {{ $json.user_id }}.
  3. Edit Fields: return reply and handover (true or false).

HL · Telegram adapter

  1. Telegram Trigger (message).
  2. IF the message has text; anything else gets "please type your message".
  3. Edit Fields: channel = telegram, user_id = tg-{{ $json.message.chat.id }}, text = {{ $json.message.text }}.
  4. Execute Sub-workflow: SUB · Sage Desk brain.
  5. Telegram · Send Message to the same chat ID, text = {{ $json.reply }}.

Test: ask the same five questions from your Boss 4 evaluation set and compare the replies with last week's. Then open the brain's executions list: each run should show an input like user_id: tg-7781234567.

Submit: both workflows, the five before-and-after replies, and the executions screenshot.
mistakes: Copying the whole agent into the Telegram workflow instead of calling a shared sub-workflow.
Keeping the memory session key as the raw chat ID, so the tg- prefix never reaches memory.
Not passing all three inputs (channel, user_id, text), so the brain cannot tell channels apart.
Checking only that Telegram replies, without comparing answers with the Boss 4 results.
b.pass: Telegram gives the same answers as before on the Boss 4 test questions, and a screenshot of the brain's executions shows user_id values starting with tg-.
b.redo: Send it back if the agent is still inside the Telegram workflow, the user_id has no tg- prefix, or there is no before-and-after comparison.

s.answer:
Worked example: Harvest Lane on the WhatsApp Cloud API test number, with your own phone as the verified recipient.

HL · WhatsApp adapter: WhatsApp Trigger (messages) → IF text message (statuses such as sent, delivered and read stop here) → Edit Fields: channel = whatsapp, user_id = wa- plus the sender's phone (path copied from the trigger output) → Execute Sub-workflow: SUB · Sage Desk brain → WhatsApp Business Cloud · Send, from the test phone number ID, text = reply. Every incoming text also updates last_customer_msg_at on the customer row.

Template (WhatsApp Manager): name order_ready, category Utility, English: "Hello {{1}}, your Harvest Lane order {{2}} is on its way and should arrive {{3}}. Reply here if you have any questions."

Order-dispatched branch: IF opted_in is false → stop. Then a Code node:

const hours = (Date.now() - new Date($json.last_customer_msg_at)) / 36e5;
return { ...$json, path: hours < 24 ? 'free-form' : 'template' };

Switch on path: free-form → Send message; template → Send Template order_ready with name, order ID and arrival time.

Test log

OrderLast messagePathResult
HL-T01Message the test number, then dispatch 5 minutes laterfree-formArrived
HL-T02Stored time set to 30 hours agotemplate (order_ready, utility)Arrived

The template path always works because templates are allowed outside the window. Never test the free-form path on a customer whose window has closed: it fails. Keep the token in an n8n credential, and replace the temporary token before it expires.
mistakes: Letting delivery and read receipts reach the brain, so the agent replies twice or answers receipts.
Trying a free-form message outside the 24-hour window instead of the approved utility template.
Creating the order update as a marketing template instead of a utility template.
Skipping the opt-in check before sending a business-initiated message.
Pasting the access token into a node instead of an n8n credential.
s.pass: Two execution screenshots, one taking the free-form path inside 24 hours and one taking the template path, both delivered to the verified number, plus a log line naming the template and its category (utility) and approval status.
s.redo: Send it back if both updates took the same path, the template is in the wrong category or unapproved, receipts are not filtered, or a token appears in plain text.

g.answer:
Worked example: a voice prototype for Harvest Lane on a voice-agent platform's free trial. The figures below are a sample; read yours from the platform's usage page.

Opening line: "Hello, this is Harvest Lane's AI assistant. I can help with opening hours, delivery areas and order status. Say 'person' at any time and Tolu will call you back." No recording without asking first.

Tool: get_order_status → POST to the n8n webhook with order_id; n8n returns one short sentence in under a second. Answers are kept under 25 words.

CallCallerSettingWorked?LengthCost
1ToluQuiet officeYes1:20from dashboard
2Restaurant managerKitchenYes1:45from dashboard
3Customer in her 70sHomeYes, slowly2:40from dashboard
4RiderBodija marketNo: noise cut in1:10from dashboard
5Student, PidginHostelYes1:35from dashboard

Success: 4 of 5. Average length: 1 min 42 s. Cost per call: total trial spend ÷ 5.

Three biggest problems: market noise triggered false interruptions; order numbers said in Pidgin were misheard twice; a 2-second pause while the webhook ran made callers repeat themselves.

Recommendation: go, for a narrow pilot only (hours, delivery areas, order status, "call me back"), with a person on offer. No-go for taking orders by voice until noise handling improves.

Submit: the call table, the platform config, the webhook workflow and this recommendation.
mistakes: Testing only with themselves in a quiet room, with no older caller and no noisy setting.
Leaving out the AI disclosure or the offer of a person.
Reporting cost per minute from the pricing page instead of actual cost per call from usage.
Giving the voice agent risky jobs such as refunds or negotiating prices.
Writing 'it works well' with no go or no-go decision.
g.pass: Notes for five real calls (including an older caller and a noisy place) show at least four successes, the opening line discloses AI and offers a person, and the notes give success rate, average length, cost per call, three problems and a clear go or no-go.
g.redo: Send it back if fewer than five people were tested, the disclosure or person option is missing, costs are guessed rather than measured, or there is no recommendation.
